concept: PieChart is a round dial cut into a recessed window: the whole is a ring or disc, each part is a slice printed in an ink pattern with its name and share tied to it by a hairline, and a legend of names repeats them as rows a finger can reach, so shares read without any hue and every slice is reachable by keys and by a table.

default_to_avoid.pattern: pie chart of rainbow slices with percentages inside the wedges, an exploded slice on hover and a legend of coloured dots
default_to_avoid.why_not: Slices told apart by hue alone fail anyone who cannot see the hue and spend colour across a unit that keeps one orange part, while text inside thin wedges collides and hover-only values leave out keyboard users.

default_to_avoid.pattern: donut chart drawn as stacked coloured arcs with a tooltip as the only place that says the numbers
default_to_avoid.why_not: P4 says a mark that shows a value exposes it as text, so every part prints its name and share, a readout says the active part and a hidden table holds the numbers.

references.source: Braun SK 4 record player (Dieter Rams, 1956): a round dial face read against printed divisions, no colour to decode
Florence Nightingale's polar area diagrams: shares told by position and printed figures, with the key set beside the drawing
Edward Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information: label the parts directly and keep the ink for the data

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The ring sits in one recessed window with elevation.well and surface.sunken, so the chart reads as a display cut into the unit and not a card laid on it.

derivation.consequence: their field is a rectangle or circle that nests in the body
derivation.form: The ring is a circle that sits inside the rectangular window with an even margin all round, and its hole nests in the ring at a fixed ratio.

derivation.consequence: a lit level uses ink at full step, never orange
derivation.form: Every slice is outlined in full step ink and filled with ink or an ink pattern, so no slice, leader or label uses action.accent or any hue.

derivation.consequence: exposes it as text to assistive tech
derivation.form: Each slice prints its name and share beside the ring, a live readout says the active slice in words, and a visually hidden table holds every value for screen readers.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Each row of the legend is at least the control size tall and picks its own slice when pressed, so a thin slice is still easy to reach.

derivation.consequence: arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends
derivation.form: The chart takes one tab stop; the arrow keys step slice by slice round the ring, and Home and End reach the first and the last slice.
New data redraws the slices in place with no sweeping animation, so there is nothing to switch off under reduce motion.

options.name: a donut in a recessed window with leader lines to printed names, the total in the hole and a legend of names under it
a ring of sixty ticks lit by share, parts told by tick length, like a rotary scale
a whole pie with the name and percentage printed in a label inside each wedge

variants.reason: A prints every name and share outside the ring on a leader so thin slices never collide, uses the hole for the total, and tells parts apart by pattern; B reads as a second Rotary and gives only sixty coarse steps with no names, and C crowds its labels inside small wedges where they overlap.

root.why: The chart fills the inline size of its column and keeps its block size whatever the data says, so the layout does not reflow when shares change.

header.why: The printed title sits on the inset line above the window, aligned to its start edge, like the label above a fader.

title.why: The title is printed in the label size and regular weight, flat ink with no emphasis, like the name above Meter.

window.why: The ring sits in a recess with inverse light and a hairline edge in line.ring that holds 3:1 against the body, at a fixed block size so a hover or a focus never moves the chart.

svg.why: The drawing is the single tab stop of the chart and takes the arrow, Home and End keys, with no tab stop per slice.

slice.why: A slice is outlined in full step ink and filled with an ink pattern, so parts differ by texture and not by hue.

focusMark.why: The keyboard mark is a ring drawn round the active slice with a gap, in the focus ring ink, so focus is a shape round the part and not a tint.

lead.why: A leader is a hairline of secondary ink with one bend that ties a slice to its printed name, a relation that is drawn and never crosses a label.

label.why: Each part prints its name and share at the caption size in regular weight, in tabular figures, beside the ring.

center.why: The total in the hole is a figure in medium weight and tabular numerals, the one big reading of the donut.

centerCaption.why: The word under the total names it, at the smallest size step in secondary ink, as a unit sits beside an LCD value.

legend.why: The legend lists every part by name beside its own pattern swatch, so the pattern is decoded in words and a part too thin to label still has a row.

item.why: Each legend row is at least the control size tall, so it is a full touch target that picks its slice when pressed.

swatch.why: The swatch is a small copy of the slice pattern in an outlined rectangle, so it matches without hue.

name.why: The part name is printed at the caption size in primary ink, regular weight.

figure.why: The value and share at the end of a legend row use tabular figures so the column keeps its width as the data changes.

readout.why: The readout is a polite live region under the window that says the active slice in words, such as Kitchen: 18 kWh, 18%, and is never a control.

table.why: A real table of the same numbers is clipped out of sight and kept for assistive tech, so the data never lives only in the drawing.

tileBg.why: The ground of every pattern tile is the sunken surface, so the hatch, the dots and the lines read as printing on the recess.

tileInk.why: Hatch and line patterns are strokes of full step ink at the ring width, a texture that survives a greyscale print.

tileDot.why: The dot pattern uses full step ink discs, a third texture next to the hatch and the lines.

tileSolid.why: The solid pattern is a full step ink fill, the one dense texture, so the first part stands out against the lighter ones.

data-active.why: The active slice, from keys or a pointer, takes a ring-width outline in place of the hairline and its legend row prints in medium weight, cues that are a line weight and a type weight and not a colour.

data-idle.why: Before any slice is active the readout shows the key hint in secondary ink, and the value in primary ink once one is.

focus-visible.why: The focus ring round the active slice is drawn only when the keyboard has focus, so a pointer press does not leave a ring.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the window, slices, patterns and the ring use system colours so the data and the active slice survive.
